label: Exponents & Radicals
overview: Exponent rules let you simplify expressions like x³ · x² or (x²)³ without expanding. Radicals (square roots, cube roots) are related to fractional exponents: √x = x^(1/2). SAT Advanced Math questions require fluency with all exponent laws, converting between radical and exponential form, and simplifying complex expressions.

steps.title: Apply the power rule to the numerator
steps.content: Raise each factor inside the parentheses to the power 2.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding exponents when raising a power to a power: (x²)³ = x⁵
commonMistakes.fix: Raising a power to a power means MULTIPLY the exponents: (x²)³ = x⁶.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying the product rule across different bases: x² · y³ = (xy)⁵
commonMistakes.fix: The product rule only works when the base is the same: x² · x³ = x⁵, but x² · y³ cannot be combined.

quickTip: Write out the rule name before applying it: 'product rule — add exponents.' This one extra second of intentionality prevents most exponent errors.
